1.  26-55569  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Continuum of Care (CoC) Board

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member Shuford, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  10 Amick, Diles III, Martins, McFadzen, Rockenbach, Topolewski, Scott,
  Shuford, Wee, Muñoz
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 4 Boyce, Brown-Shock, Lock, Tan

2.  26-55570  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on local strategy to respond to

the FY 2026 Continuum of Care (CoC) Program Notice of Funding Opportunity
(NOFO).

A motion was made by Member Amick, seconded by Member Rockenbach, to
approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

Yes:  10 Amick, Diles III, Martins, McFadzen, Rockenbach, Topolewski, Scott,
  Shuford, Wee, Muñoz
No:  0 None
Recused: 0 None
Abstain: 0 None
Absent: 4 Boyce, Brown-Shock, Lock, Tan

  • Health Department staff member Joseph Botelho provided an update on the
  purpose and function of the Ranking Policy and Reallocation Policy. He
  reviewed feedback received from subrecipients during office hours, along
  with staff recommendations. The discussion focused on the ranking process
  and strategy, as well as the proposed reallocation thresholds and strategy.
  Joseph acknowledged that these are difficult conversations due to the
  federal funding structure and emphasized that no decisions are made lightly.
  He also reiterated that staff will continue working to minimize displacement of
  people experiencing homelessness while preserving Continuum of Care
  funding.
  • HUD requires CoCs to demonstrate a single, coordinated, inclusive, and
  outcome-oriented community process for the solicitation, objective review,
  ranking, and selection of project applications.
  • Project ranking is used to determine what projects are more protected, that
  would be either Tier 1 or Tier 2. There are different approaches to ranking,
  historically overall we have done an overall weighted ranking. Used to allow
  very high functioning transitional housing projects to be ranked high,
  • HUD requires CoCs to have a reallocation process as part of the CoC
  Program Competition, but does not generally require you to reallocate.
  • HUD will conditionally select project applications for funding in this order:
  o CoC planning and UFA costs
  o Tier 1
  o DV Bonus
  o Permanent Housing for Families with Children
  o New TH and SSO Projects
  o Other projects
  • FY 2026 CoC NOFO funding available= $4.04B
  • After estimated Tier 1 awards, $1.73B remains available for projects in Tier
  2.
  • HSB hosted a CoC subrecipient office hours, provided an overview on the

  Page 2 of 6
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, JULY 14, 2026
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810

  NOFO, and instructions to complete the RFP. Additionally, there was
  discussion on strategies and best practices for devolping a competitive
  application. No oral feedback was provided, two polls were completed by
  participants the questions asked during the poll:
  o Should the CoC reallocate partially unspent funds from renewal
  projects to maximize teh number of projects included in the FY 2026
  HUD submission?
  o How should the CoC balance project performance scores with project
  type when determining the Priority Listing?
  • Strategies that are being recommended in the memo include:
  • Reallocate and Transition:
  o Recommendation 1: Transition Tier 2 Funding
  o Recommendation 2: Transition Rapid Rehousing to Transitional
  Housing
  o Reecommendation 3: Preserve Rapid Rehousing Capacity
  • Rank and Prioritize
  o Recommendation 4: Rank by Project Type and Performance
  Threshold
  o Recommendation 5: Reallocate Projected Unspent Funds
  o Recommendation 6: Prioritize Transition Projects over New Projects
  • Ranking by project type and threshold helps establish a minimum
  performance threshold before project-type prioritization is applied, it supports
  strategic Tier 1 placement, and responds to FY 2026 fundiing risk because
  40% ARD is in competitive Tier 2.
  • The estimated FY 2026 CoC NOFO estimated funding available was
  discussed. Memebrs of board have questions regarding Tier 1 and 2 funding.
  • The FY 2026 Scoring and reallocation results were discussed by project
  type.
  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provided additional comments regarding the
  top priorities that staff are looking into as staff naviagte through this.
  • Staff and board members discussed Rapid rehousing and Transitional
  rehousing along with additonal comments regarding this item.
  • A member of the public commented that the shallow subsidy program was
  not mentioned. They expressed that they believe the program is an important
  component of enhancing and supporting permanent housing opportunities.

  Continuum of Care (CoC) FY 2026 Scoring and Ranking Policy.

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member Martins, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  10 Amick, Diles III, Martins, McFadzen, Rockenbach, Topolewski, Scott,

  • Health Department Staff Joseph Botelho provided a brief update on the CoC
  Scoring and Ranking, one correction made was clarifying that cost
  effectiveness does include match. Some language was removed around
  what HUD. The primary thing that was added was the Summary of Draft
  Ranking Policy updates ranking by trhreshold.
  • The only update was adding the ranking system by project type and
  includinig the 70% threshold, there will be more discussion on whether the
  70% is appropriate or it can be lowered to 65%.
  • Member Amick requested clarification on the ranking of section three, staff
  provided additonal guidance.

4.  26-55572  Recommendation to review and approve proposed updates to the Long Beach
  Continuum of Care (CoC) Reallocation Policies and Procedures.

  A motion was made by Member Martins, seconded by Member Rockenbach,
  to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  10 Amick, Diles III, Martins, McFadzen, Rockenbach, Topolewski, Scott,
  Shuford, Wee, Muñoz
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 4 Boyce, Brown-Shock, Lock, Tan

  • Health Department Staff Joseph Botelho provided a brief update on the
  Reallocation policies and procedures, added System-Level or Portfolio-
  Based Reallocation. This would allow the CoC to consider portfolio-wide
  reallocation strategies using objective expenditure, utilization, performance,
  or NOFO related data. The language was added to clarify reallocation
  exemptions and the appeal process. This is meant to help with future
  conversations and decion making.
  • The board had no further questions regarding this item.

5.  26-55573  Recommendation to discuss proposed revisions to the Long Beach Continuum of
  Care (CoC) Board composition, including the potential addition of new CoC Board
  seats.

  Page 4 of 6

  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810

  A motion was made by Member Scott, seconded by Member Shuford, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  10 Amick, Diles III, Martins, McFadzen, Rockenbach, Topolewski, Scott,
  Shuford, Wee, Muñoz
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 4 Boyce, Brown-Shock, Lock, Tan

  • Health Department staff member Joseph Botelho provided an update on the
  Long Beach Continuum of Care (CoC) Charter and Bylaws. No additional
  edits had been made since the previous meeting in June. The discussion
  focused on providing additional information regarding the proposed
  expansion of the CoC Board through the addition of nine new board seats.
  • Staff explained that the FY 2026 Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO)
  awards up to eight points for having a representative CoC governance
  board. Staff and members expressed concerns that adding nine seats would
  increase the total board membership to 25. However, they also
  acknowledged that earning these additional points could strengthen the
  CoC's funding application and improve its competitiveness for project
  funding. Overall, both staff and members agreed that maximizing the
  available NOFO points is an important priority.
  • Member Amick left the meeting after the final vote.
  • A member of the public provoided information regarding a law enforcement
  officer that would be interested in being a part of the CoC Board.
  .

6.  26-55574  Recommendation to review and approve proposed updates to the Long Beach
  Continuum of Care (CoC) Governance Charter and Bylaws, including revisions to
  the CoC Board composition.

  A motion was made by Member Rockenbach, seconded by Member Shuford,
  to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9 Diles III, Martins, McFadzen, Rockenbach, Topolewski, Scott,
  Shuford, Wee, Muñoz
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 5 Amick, Boyce, Brown-Shock, Lock, Tan

  Page 5 of 6
   LONG BEACH CONTINUUM OF CARE MINUTES
  TUESDAY, JULY 14, 2026
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 2:00 PM

  • City staff advised the Board that this item was to finalize approval of one of
  the two proposed Governance Charter and Bylaws versions presented under
  Item 5. Option 1 did not include the additional board seats discussed in the
  previous agenda item, while Option 2 included the proposed additional seats.
  • Board Member McFadzen moved to approve the redlined version of the
  Governance Charter and Bylaws that included the additional board seats.
  Board Member Shufford seconded the motion.
  • A roll call vote was conducted, and the motion passed with nine members
  voting in favor.

PUBLIC COMMENT

  • No public comment.

  • No announcements.
